Curriculum
Ensuring the very best outcomes for all our children and families is embedded in our practice at Chertsey Nursery School. We are committed to empowering every child to reach their full personal and learning potential.
We recognise and value each child as a unique individual. There is a strong and sustained focus on meeting individual needs, with personal, social and emotional development at the heart of everything we do. Our practice fully reflects the principles of the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) Statutory Framework, ensuring that all children are supported to learn, develop and thrive. Our aim is to provide a secure and inspiring foundation that supports children’s future life chances and readiness for the next stage of education.
We offer a rich, enabling indoor and outdoor environment that promotes curiosity, independence and a love of learning. Children are encouraged to investigate, explore and ask questions, while we ensure that safeguarding and welfare are always prioritised.

Curriculum Intent
Our curriculum intent is based on appropriate learning needs of two, three and four year olds. Our aim is to provide a broad and balanced curriculum where the children can access learning opportunities which promote high expectations, risk taking and independence through a combination of adult-led and child-initiated activities. These equip the children with the motivation, skills and attitudes needed for life. The needs of each individual are carefully planned to ensure the best possible outcomes.Accordion content
Curriculum Intention
The environment is carefully planned to support the implementation of the curriculum and promote learning. This enables the children to be independent and autonomous in their learning both inside and outside. The children are taught to take responsibility for their own learning and practise the skills they have been taught through their own child initiated learning. Adults are deployed in the provision to ‘tune in’ to the children to support, intervene, extend play and ask inciteful questions. The role of the adults is key, as this will support further planning opportunities by adding resources and activities to extend their play and learning. In order to teach key skills, specific activities are planned and delivered using an adult (adult-led activities). Learning intentions for these are written onto the daily planning sheet and colour coded linked to the seven areas of learning. Specific skills and knowledge is also taught daily through ‘group times’. Group times promote specific language and literacy skills and knowledge . There are also planned opportunities for specific interventions to be provided for children who may need additional support. These may be individual or small group and delivered either within and alongside a child’s play, or in a more quiet, calm space.
Curriulum Impact
The impact of our curriculum will be demonstrated by the milestones* that our children achieve. Daily observations of children will inform our daily practice and planning for each individual. At specific moments during each academic year, the children will be assessed against the milestone for their age. For those individual children who are not meeting their milestones, targeted plans will be implemented to support their progress. For those children who are not on a mainstream pathway, or have enhanced levels of Early Intervention (Funding), progress for these individuals will be tracked through their personal support plans and targets.
*Milestones adapted and support by the principles of OPAL Observing Play and Learning, developed by The Barnet Early Years Alliance.

Early Years Pupil Premium
From April 2015, the Government introduced additional funding for early years settings to help improve the education provided for disadvantaged children. This funding is known as the Early Years Pupil Premium (EYPP).
To be eligible for EYPP, children must be accessing their funded early education entitlement. If you meet at least one of the criteria below, we may be able to access additional funding to support your child during their time at nursery:
If you believe you meet any of these criteria, please speak to the office or the Headteacher. We will provide you with the necessary information and help you apply so that your child can benefit from this additional support.
Please check out our reports below to see how we use the money to give every child the best start.

Parent-Friendly FAQs
1. Does EYPP affect my benefits? No, claiming EYPP does not affect any benefits you receive. It is additional funding for the nursery, not a payment to you.
2. How do I apply? It’s simple! Speak to the nursery office or the Headteacher, and we will guide you through the process. We just need a few details to check eligibility.
3. What is the funding used for? The funding is used to provide extra resources, staff training, and enrichment activities to support your child’s learning and development.
4. Will my child be treated differently? Absolutely not. EYPP funding is used to enhance opportunities for all children, ensuring everyone benefits from a high-quality learning environment.

Special Educational Needs and Disabilties
We are fully committed to the inclusion of all children and believe that this is beneficial to both the mainstream children and those with special needs that they play and learn together. We have long experience and expertise in working with children with varying special needs, and involve the parents, who know their child best, in every aspect of the child’s learning at nursery.
We have the skills and expertise to educate children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) in either our mainstream or our specialist class. Our specialist class supports children with identified complex needs. To find out more about the admissions process, please view our Admissions Policy.
Our specialist class can support children with a variety of additional needs, including autism. Children may have mild physical difficulties and speech language and communication needs.
To view our SEND Policy, SEND Information Report or Surrey Local Offer, please click on the appropriate links. Surrey County Council can be contacted for advice and support, contact the Surrey Learners Single Point of Access on 0300 200 1015.

Understanding Funded Entitlements
There are different types of funded entitlement for two, three and four year olds which are all accepted at Chertsey Nursery School.
Funded entitlement for two year olds
There are two different types of funded entitlements for two year olds. Early Learning for Two Year Olds, previously known as FEET (Funded Entitlement for Eligible Two-year olds) and Working Entitlement for two year olds.
Early Learning for Two Year Olds Funding
This funding is for 2-year-olds of families in receipt of specific benefits, or those who meet one of the additional criteria listed below.
Early Learning for Two Year Old funding offers eligible families up to 15 hours of funded early education a week for 38 weeks a year.
At Chertsey Nursery School we accept and prioritise these places for children. These are offered over five morning or five afternoon sessions per week. You will need a valid code to be able to access a place. To apply for a code, visit the Surrey County Council Website. If you are not able to access the online application, then we can help with applications. Do pop in and see us!
Working Entitlement for two year olds
Most working parents of two year olds are able to access 30 hours per week of funded early education. Parents (both parents in a two parent household) or one parent in a single parent household need to be earning between the National Minimum Living Wage and £100,000 each to be eligible.
To find out more, visit the Best Start in Life website.
At Chertsey Nursery School, we offer the 30 hours working entitlement for two year olds over five days, Monday to Friday. You will need to provide an 11 digit code that you can get from the Best Start in Life website.

Funded entitlement for three and four year olds
From the term after a child turns three years old, all children are entitled to 15 hours of early education per week. This is called Universal entitlement. At Chertsey Nursery School we offer this over five morning or five afternoon sessions.
Working Entitlement for three and four year olds
Most working parents of three and four year olds are able to access an additional 15 hours per week of funded early education (which totals 30 hours). Parents (both parents in a two parent household) or one parent in a single parent household need to be earning between the National Minimum Living Wage and £100,000 each to be eligible.
To find out more, visit the Best Start in Life website.
At Chertsey Nursery School, we offer the 30 hours working entitlement for two year olds over five days, Monday to Friday. You will need to provide an 11 digit code that you can get from the Best Start in Life website.

Welcome to Chertsey Nursery School! We are proud to offer high-quality early years education for children aged 2, 3, and 4 years old, and have been at the heart of the Chertsey community for over 50 years. Our nurturing environment is led by specially trained early years practitioners, where children are encouraged to explore, experiment, and develop a lifelong love of learning.

To learn more, please explore our website or contact us to arrange a visit—we would love to welcome you in person.
Since September 2018, we have been in an exciting partnership with Dorking Nursery School, which has achieved Outstanding in its last seven Ofsted inspections. This collaboration strengthens both schools, supporting our development and financial sustainability, and ensuring we continue to provide the very best for our children and families.
Our Executive Headteacher, Donna Harwood-Duffy, works across both Chertsey and Dorking, bringing a wealth of expertise in early education. At Chertsey, Head of School Anita Cheeseman leads the day-to-day operations, ensuring that every child and family receives the support they need.

Admissions
Below you can see a short video about our nursery as well as further information on our provision.
We welcome applications from parents and carers at any time. Applications can be made directly online using our online application form. We advise families to read our Admissions Policy prior to completing their application. All places are offered in line with the Surrey Admissions Policy for Nursery Schools.
To complete an online application, please click here.
Admissions information
Our fees are reviewed annually.
Admission to the 2s Nursery
Our 2-3s Nursery is open in the morning and afternoon. Depending on how children are being funded as to the sessions that are offered. All places are allocated in line with the admissions criteria detailed in our Admissions Policy.
Any hours over and above these sessions are charged at a fee and are subject to availability. Fees are updated and reviewed annually.
*families must be able to provide the valid funding code for a WPE or Early Learning for Two year olds place. See our Understanding funded entitlements page for more information.
Admissions to the 3s Nursery
All places are allocated in line with the admissions criteria detailed in our Admissions Policy. All three and four year old are eligible for Universal Funded entitlement of 15 hours per week.
Children are allocated either a morning (8.30am to 11.30am) or afternoon (12.15pm to 3.15pm) place. Working Parent Entitlement* places are 8.30am - 2.30pm. Sessions are funded and children must attend five sessions per week Monday to Friday.
Any hours over and above these sessions are charged at a fee and are subject to availability. Fees are updated and reviewed annually.
*families must be able to provide the valid funding code for a WPE place. See our Understanding funded entitlements page for more information.
Additional Sessions in the 2-3s and 3-5s Nursery
Any sessions outside of funded entitlement are subject to a fee, see above. Fees are reviewed and updated annually.
Lunch club - available Monday to Friday, 11.30am - 12.15pm. Price includes a hot school lunch.
Extended day - available Monday to Friday 8.30am - 12.15pm or 11.30am - 3.15pm.
Late pick up - available Monday to Friday 2.30pm - 3.15pm.
Admissions under SEND criteria 2
Admissions for children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities are made directly to the school in the same way as above for all children. Parents wishing their child to be considered for a place under Admissions Criteria 2, (Social, medical, additional or special need) will need to indicate this on their application form and submit supporting evidence from relevant professionals, such as paediatricians, speech and language therapists, etc. For more information about Special Educational Needs and Disabilities at Chertsey Nursery School, please visit our SEND page.
